body.p: Now I will tell you a tale. A tale that I have recorded once. My tale. Its name is Last Year's Summer. An old man Selkup lives on a shore of a lake. He catches fish. Sometimes he chops firewood for himself. He brings water for himself. So he lives. Oh, at some time his tent wanted to move. The old man thinks, what's this, what happened? He went out of his tent. Oh, a big hairy old man is coming here. The old man, I will eat you know! Oh, don't eat me! Live here! I will feed you. So.[ShA:] ÉÉtaÉ¡odazÊ is an unexpected form, ÉÉtaÉ¡ozazÊ is expected. They began to live. So they live. A huge old man sometimes he works. Sometimes he would bring firewood. Sometimes he would bring water. They do eat fish. There is fish in their lake, after all. A bit for eating. They live. One day the old man says, the big old man, the hairy old man says. "The old man, what's your name?" The old man says. "My name, my name is the Last year's summer." The old man says again: "What's your name?" "As I said, my name is Last year's summer." Last year's summer. The autumn came. There left very few fish in their river. They didn't have any food. There will be no left soon. Well, what one should do? The old man said. "The old man, now I will eat you!" The old man said. "Don't eat me! Now I will bring you caviar here. I have a huge barrel of caviar there." He brought it. The huge old man took that barrel from the two sides. So he started at once drinking it from the edges. Then he raised it up. He raised it. The old man Selkup without thinking. That, so he hit him from above with the head of the ax. And he ran away. He ran far away. The giant, that huge old man with a hairy body, his cry. Is really terrible. He screams very loudly, he screams very loudly. At his cry. A huge old man with big eyes came running. "Oh, you are here! And who did this to you?" And the old man said. The old man with a hairy body said. "The Last year's summer, the Last year's summer. Oho!" "Where are we going to find the people who left last year? They have left far away, after all. How would you do it? You can't catch up with the people who left last year. They have left far away!" So, that's the end. And now I'm going to tell you another story. (â¦). The name of this tale is "The old woman who plaits the tendons." A tent. An old woman is sitting in the tent. The old woman is plaiting the tendons. Oh, at some time an old woman entered the tent. A very scary old woman. "Old woman, old woman, what are you doing?" "I am plaiting the threads." "And what if we plait the threads together?" "Okay." "Now I will go to take my tendon." "Well, go, take it." These. The old woman stayed. After the old scary woman left. She got into the bed curtains quickly. All the people on the bed. She smeared them with â¦ fat. At some time, this old woman, a scary old woman. She came, one can hear. Tendons of big bulls are there in her basin. Well. She lost that old woman, after all. "Oh, where did that old woman go?!" She got into the bed curtains. She entered the bed curtains. People are sleeping in the bed curtains. The old woman is sleeping. It seems that all their foreheads perspired. Oh, at seems, that people have been sleeping for a long time. Well, let them sleep.[ShA:] KÉdÊ²idaraxaÊ is an unexpected form, kÉdÊ²izaraxaÊ is expected. She went out of the bed curtains. She went to the other side. The old woman is also sleeping at the opposite side. Everyone she lives with are sleeping. They have no sweat. "A, she has cheated me! That old woman." In the morning. The people woke up. Those who lived with the old woman who plaited the tendons woke up. And those on the other side are asleep. And why are they sleeping on the other side? Look then, why are they sleeping? When he entered the bed curtains. These were all killed. That's the end. NEE060009
